newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistan to set up camp for new Afghan refugees.
newsitem.headline: Pakistan to set up camp for new Afghan refugees.

text.p: Pakistani authorities said on Tuesday that a new camp would be set up outside the northwestern town of Peshawar to house refugees fleeing fighting in eastern Afghanistan.

A government statement said the United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees would supply tents for the camp at Nasir Bagh and seek non-governmental organisations' help with food and other "basic assistance" for the refugees.
Pakistan says it has closed its border with eastern Afghanistan after the outbreak of fighting there last week.

But Pakistani commissioner for Afghan refugees, Rustam Shah Mohmand, said on Tuesday about 800 refugee families had arrived after the main eastern town of Jalalabad fell to the rebel Taleban Islamic militia last Wednesday.
Afghan sources in Pakistan said more than 6,000 Afghans had crossed into Pakistan in the past five days.
Mohmand said people had fled Jalalabad fearing bombing by government jets. Taleban is fighting to topple the Kabul government and impose a strict Islamic order.
Pakistan hosted more than three million Afghan refugees during the Soviet occupation of their country in 1980s and many of them are still living here.
